description: Knowledge of how to critically review and validate outputs generated by automated systems, including use of digital dashboards, error/QA logs, and exception workflows.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Role shifts from primarily hands-on editorial tasks to QA, validation, and meta-review of AI/digital system-generated outputs. Officer is now a reviewer of automated product and output templates, focusing on compliance, appropriateness, and robust metadata rather than manual edits.
justification: Officer must understand and critically evaluate AI-generated reports, ensuring they align with standards and user needs, rather than producing/editing content manually.

description: Understanding of how data and products must be formatted, described, tagged, and validated for machine and human discoverability/reuse; ability to check compliance with APIs and metadata frameworks.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Role shifts from primarily hands-on editorial tasks to QA, validation, and meta-review of AI/digital system-generated outputs. Officer is now a reviewer of automated product and output templates, focusing on compliance, appropriateness, and robust metadata rather than manual edits.
justification: Officer will oversee machine-actionable output production; thus, must ensure outputs meet new interoperability and metadata standards.

development area: Digital product specification/interfacing with AI systems
description: Ability to configure or specify AI/digital system generation of custom outputs based on user/client need, including interactive input to templates or automated workflows.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Interprets client information requests to create custom statistical tabulations.'
change to work: Less focus on manual tabulation, more on translating requests into system specifications or configurations, specifying requirements for AI-generated custom tables (filters, formats), or approving/excluding custom visualizations based on user capability.
justification: Role now requires the ability to translate non-technical requirements into specifications for automated systems—effectively serving as a product configurator and validator.

description: Familiarity with new data/metadata validation routines (metadata completeness, open-data readiness, API compliance) for dissemination artifacts.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
change to work: Emphasis pivots toward evaluating metadata integrity, machine-actionability, and fitness-for-output in digital-first dissemination systems as well as traditional data quality.
justification: Officer must review not just data, but the metadata, actionable format, and accessibility of digital outputs, requiring knowledge of modern metadata/data validation.

description: Skill in reviewing, editing, and contextualizing auto-produced documentation, and creating user guidance on AI-enabled products/delivery platforms.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: Communication: 'Drafts reports and articles...; Drafts program information manuals and training packages...'
change to work: With major documentation and outputs auto-generated by AI, the Officer will shift to reviewing, adapting, and contextualizing AI-generated documentation for clarity or compliance, as well as preparing end-user training on new automated dissemination workflows.
justification: Officer must shift from creating documentation to reviewing/adapting AI-generated manuals and preparing training for next-gen dissemination tools.

description: Ability to articulate requirements for automated compilation and visualize/review the resulting products for both internal compliance and user fit-for-purpose.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output.'
change to work: Compiling and generating outputs is substantially automated; the focus becomes configuring requirements for system-driven compilation and reviewing outputs for appropriateness and user need.
justification: Systematically understanding how to specify requirements for and audit outputs created by AI—rather than doing the work directly.

description: Familiarity with open metadata, API-first platforms, discoverability protocols, and digital product design/selection as part of the output management process.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 5. Contextual knowledge: 'Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada...', 'Knowledge of the divisional mandate... to adhere to various statistical and administrative practices... marketing and dissemination of statistical data.'
change to work: Expanding contextual knowledge to include awareness of metadata API, open data, and digital workflow standards relevant to dissemination and output selection.
justification: Officer needs not only source/data context, but strong knowledge of open metadata, discoverability, and standards for modern digital dissemination.

description: Skill in reviewing automation pipelines and the configuration/operation of modular dissemination components, including versioning, audit logging, and standards checks.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Shifts to ensuring QA, machine-actionability, and compliance of outputs published by automated dissemination modules; less manual formatting or ad hoc release, more focus on confirming process consistency and standards adherence.
justification: Tracking modular, automated digital components rather than managing outputs individually requires technical QA/oversight skills.

description: Knowledge of best practices and technical requirements for API-ready, modular, and automation-compliant output creation and management.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Shifts to ensuring QA, machine-actionability, and compliance of outputs published by automated dissemination modules; less manual formatting or ad hoc release, more focus on confirming process consistency and standards adherence.
justification: Outputs are now consumed by APIs, digital partners, and AI systems, not just humans; officer must understand their requirements.

description: Working knowledge of open data standards, APIs, metadata protocols, and automated/digital system QA.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
change to work: In addition to traditional quality review, must assess if dissemination components and their data products are compliant with open standards, machine-readable formats, robust metadata, and can be consumed/triggered using APIs and digital platforms.
justification: Need to technically review not just contents but interoperability, format, and metadata quality of digital outputs.

description: Able to communicate digital dissemination requirements to system developers, test new modules, and flag QA/process/standards issues as part of agile teams.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.'
change to work: Involvement shifts toward technical and process consultation—helping design, troubleshoot, and refine modular, automated dissemination infrastructure as part of team efforts, not manual product assembly.
justification: Must collaborate with IT, systems specialists, and automation engineers.

development area: Training in automation and digital dissemination
description: Knowledge and ability to explain the operation, limitations, and QA of automation-based dissemination, including use of API endpoints, automated version control, and exception handling.
historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.'
change to work: Contributes to and delivers training on automated dissemination systems, API-based delivery, use of modular tools, and standards compliance, rather than only manual process guides.
justification: Materials and training now focus on automation systems, not “manual how-to.”

description: Skill in systematically reviewing and validating AI/LLM-generated analytics, summaries, dashboards, ensuring clarity, rigor, and fitness for purpose.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Focuses on editing/validating draft outputs auto-generated by AI/LLM systems, with less hands-on original creation of content. Increases the need for critical review and QA of analytics and narrative reports.
justification: Officer must be able to review, correct, and approve machine-generated outputs, which requires understanding both their structure and potential errors/limitations.

description: Knowledge of how to review, edit, and translate AI/LLM-produced documentation for clarity, appropriateness, and full methodological transparency.
historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.'
change to work: Role changes from manual drafting to reviewing and contextualizing AI-generated reports/articles, ensuring methodological accuracy, narrative clarity, and client relevance.
justification: Officer must bridge between automated drafts (which may lack nuance/context) and the communication needs of diverse audiences.

development area: Critical interpretation and user-centered adaptation of AI output
description: Ability to assess machine-generated descriptive content for context, accuracy, messaging, and usability, making modifications for diverse stakeholders.
historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Summarizes and describes meaning of data.'
change to work: Instead of original summary, the officer assesses, tailors, and contextualizes AI-generated summaries for accuracy, audience comprehension, and statistical integrity.
justification: Critical thinking is needed to augment, clarify, and correct draft outputs—recognizing where the machine narrative may be insufficient or misleading.

description: Ability to read, interpret, and contextualize reports/flags produced by AI/ML-driven QA tools, and determine required follow-up action.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
change to work: Shifts from hands-on validation/checking to reviewing, adjudicating, and contextualizing automated QA results; involved in refining validation standards, thresholds, and escalation criteria.
justification: Officer needs skills in interpreting automated QA diagnostics, anomaly/outlier reports, and in setting thresholds for further action/escalation.

development area: Validation protocol analysis and system feedback
description: Skill in critically analyzing automated validation rules and procedures, suggesting improvements, and helping tune AI/ML tools for domain needs.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Reviews and assesses data quality from new and modified computer systems and databases.'
change to work: Shifts from hands-on validation/checking to reviewing, adjudicating, and contextualizing automated QA results; involved in refining validation standards, thresholds, and escalation criteria.
justification: Must play a role in system feedback—improving AI/ML QA processes based on recurring errors, edge cases, or shifting data/context.

description: Understanding of AI/ML approaches to data quality validation, anomaly detection, and benchmarking, with ability to evaluate accuracy and contextual appropriateness.
historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Analyzes and evaluates data for consistency, reliability, and appropriateness.'
change to work: Now involves oversight of automated validation, focusing on exception handling and improvement of automated benchmarking/consistency logic.
justification: Officer must know how to guide machine-driven evaluation and provide feedback loops into system learning.

description: Ability to review and resolve uncertainty in privacy/SCD actions taken by AI, including nuanced judgment in ambiguous or novel output types.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Editing and validation tasks are now centered on reviewing disclosure and privacy compliance in automated outputs; typical manual intervention is for flagged exceptions.
justification: Officer must interpret and adjudicate complex AI-flagged disclosure risks, often in new, ambiguous, or critical cases.

development area: Automated SCD systems and audit trails
description: Understanding of how privacy/SCD tools function, what is logged, and how to document, supplement, or override their actions and rationales in complex compliance scenarios.
historic work: Technical Activities/Skills: 'Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts... and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the editing, validation, marketing and dissemination of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.'
change to work: Role pivots to ensuring automation aligns with all applicable privacy/SCD legal/policy frameworks, and to documenting, auditing, and justifying human interventions for privacy compliance.
justification: The Officer must audit, validate, and, if needed, modify the rationale and documentation auto-generated by SCD tools, ensuring compliance.

development area: Output package quality assurance and sign-off
description: Ability to systematically review all components of an automated output package (narrative, metadata, technical notes, translations), and to confidently approve release or manage/resolve anomalies and exceptions.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: The focus is now on vetting and approving automation-assembled output packages (rather than preparing/disseminating them manually), intervening in special cases, and ensuring appropriate communication/documentation accompanies the release.
justification: Critical review and sign-off of complete, automation-assembled output packages (including supporting documentation and metadata) requires advanced QA oversight skills.

development area: Automated output integration and completeness review
description: Knowledge of what constitutes a complete, high-quality, and compliant automated statistical output package—including multi-lingual requirements, uncertainty metrics, and all supporting appendices.
historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables, and other output.'
change to work: Instead of compiling outputs, Officer verifies the completeness, integration, and appropriateness of automation-prepared outputs, and reviews the supporting contextual narrative and technical appendices.
justification: Increased need to understand and validate complex, multi-source output packages to ensure each element is properly incorporated and documented by automation.

development area: Digital dissemination systems oversight and troubleshooting
description: Ability to audit, validate, and escalate issues in automated dissemination pipelines—including exceptions, platform errors, or complex user access scenarios.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Duties move toward oversight and QA of automated dissemination; the Officer becomes responsible for approvals, troubleshooting, and digital platform QA, rather than hands-on dissemination tasks.
justification: Officer must monitor, diagnose, and improve automated systems, and interface across business/IT boundaries on exception scenarios.

development area: API/digital platform and metadata enrichment protocols
description: Understanding how API-delivered outputs, advanced metadata tagging, and AI-agent searchability work in modern dissemination platforms; ability to advise on standards, upgrades, and user impact.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.'
change to work: Focus of participation shifts to collaborating on digital-first workflow updates, advising on metadata enrichment and API-channel design, and supporting platform evolution and standards adoption.
justification: Deeper technical and policy knowledge required to collaborate on digital and API-first platform design, rollout, and QA.

development area: Digital dissemination user support and training expertise
description: Expertise in training/support related to API-first dissemination and real-time digital product access, for both staff and data users adapting to new digital release modalities.
historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.'
change to work: Training/support must now emphasize API and digital-first dissemination, AI discoverability, and automation-driven change management for users (internal and external).
justification: New/advanced training content is required for digital system users, focusing on automation, APIs, machine-actionable metadata, and modern dissemination workflows.

development area: Automated metadata and linkage standards and QA
description: Up-to-date knowledge of metadata standards, discoverability schemas, and the functioning of automated data/content loading and output linking systems.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata.'
change to work: Role pivots to meta-validation: checking completeness, enrichment, API/AI actionability, and automated linkage of metadata; less hands-on, more oversight/troubleshooting/reporting.
justification: Need to understand, audit, and validate compliance with digital/automated metadata, linkage, and discoverability standards.

description: Skill in supporting, diagnosing, and optimizing access to outputs for both human and automated users in a digital, API-first landscape.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
change to work: Emphasis shifts to consulting on, and troubleshooting, machine-actionable outputs, API access, and discoverability—supporting power users, developers, and advanced human/AI clients; must be able to diagnose failures in digital product access.
justification: Requirements for advanced advisory and diagnostic skills related to API, AI, and machine-actionable data use.

description: Skill in systematically reviewing, validating, and customizing AI/LLM-generated dissemination products for publication, metadata, and audience standards.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Edits, validates, markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Primary tasks now involve reviewing for adherence to publication, meta, and audience-specific standards; less generation by hand, more focus on standards QA, final adaptation, and sign-off.
justification: Must be able to interpret, critique, and adapt a wide range of AI/automation-derived outputs (text, graphics, microdata, etc.) for diverse audiences.

development area: Automated workflow and product pipeline logic
description: Understanding how automation assembles, enriches, and finalizes dissemination products; ability to give effective feedback and suggest workflow improvements for special requirements.
historic work: Technical Activities: 6. Research and analysis: 'Compiles data from diverse sources to produce statistical charts, tables and other output.'
change to work: Transition from compiling to reviewing/reshaping multi-source, automation-created outputs (including troubleshooting or specifying refinements in AI workflows for special cases, e.g., for PUMF or complex graphics).
justification: Officer must understand the system’s logic for assembling outputs and participate in feedback/improvement for the automation pipeline.

development area: Exception management and high-visibility release liaison
description: Ability to review and approve exception cases in digital orchestration systems, and to coordinate confidential/embargoed or impactful public releases with stakeholders.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Participates on data production and dissemination teams.'
change to work: Role focuses on policy review, exception workflows, and special-case product releases (e.g., embargo, retraction, or high-visibility clients), much less on routine operational work.
justification: Officer needs skills in navigating, auditing, and managing digital release workflows and exception approval, as well as in communicating with high-level clients.

development area: Secure access management and client liaison
description: Skill in granting, auditing, and managing secure digital access to confidential or embargoed data, and in advanced client communication for sensitive releases.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
change to work: Duties now center on high-level user support and consultation (e.g., secure research access, press briefings for embargoed releases, subscriber communications), as standard release channels are largely hands-free.
justification: Greater responsibility for managing access for diverse, privileged user groups in API-enabled, secure digital environments.

description: Skill in reviewing, validating, and adapting content, strategy, and channel selection generated by AI for promotional outreach, including campaign performance monitoring.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Markets and disseminates data.'
change to work: Role shifts to reviewing and optimizing AI-generated outreach campaigns across platforms, and taking ownership for sensitive or high-impact communications.
justification: Must critically evaluate and intervene on AI-prompted messages for clarity, alignment, and risk.

description: Knowledge of effective AI-driven outreach strategies, and how to review, adapt, or supplement messaging for interpretation accuracy, compliance, or complex audience needs.
historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Drafts reports and articles on the interpretation and use of statistical data and the concepts, methods and techniques used.'
change to work: Work shifts to editing/validating AI-generated language for promos and assuring correct interpretation/messaging in outreach products.
justification: Reviewing, customizing, or rejecting AI-generated marketing and communication text requires greater skill in risk assessment, narrative tone, and public/audience centricity.

description: Ability to handle, resolve, and document nuanced, ambiguous, or policy-sensitive user issues, working in tandem with automated systems and tracking knowledgebase/FAQ impacts.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Provides statistical data and consultative services to users.'
change to work: Most queries are routine and answered by automation. Officer’s consultative role is reserved for escalated, non-routine, nuanced, or strategic requests, as well as designing/curating advanced support pathways.
justification: Officer requires skill at diagnosing and resolving complex digital support issues, including those only surfaced after automation fails.

description: Proficiency in reviewing and editing AI-generated FAQ content, training staff and power users on automated support, and feeding user insights back into digital service design.
historic work: Technical Activities: Communication: 'Provides input to training material and assists in the delivery.'
change to work: Provides ongoing review of AI-generated knowledge articles, populates advanced FAQ material, and supports training/advice for both users and staff in the new automated support ecosystem.
justification: Greater need for digital literacy in chatbot/AI knowledge curation, and in content review/editing for automated support channels.
